newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt ruling party sweeps local elections.
newsitem.headline: Egypt ruling party sweeps local elections.

text.p: Egypt's ruling National Democratic Party (NDP) has won a sweeping victory in local council elections, an official said on Monday.
Opposition parties and human rights groups have accused President Hosni Mubarak's government of rigging the April 7 elections.
The NDP won 93.5 percent of the 47,382 contested provincial and local council seats, according to final results shown to Reuters by a government official.

The independents won 3.5 percent of the seats and opposition candidates 0.2 percent. Results for the remaining seats were either cancelled because of minor violations or delayed for other reasons, said the official, who did not want to be named.
The NDP had won 94 percent of seats in the country's 454-seat parliament in the 1995 general election.

NDP candidates won 54 percent of the seats even before the elections started because there were not enough opposition or independent candidates contesting them, the official said. He said about 58,000 candidates ran for the elections.

"The government and its party have stuck to the same mechanisms and methods used during the 1995 People's Assembly (parliament) general elections, in which the votes were rigged," said the independent Center for Human Rights Legal Aid (CHRLA).

"Hundreds of independents were pressured into waiving their rights as candidates. Also several security raids were carried out by the authorities over the past few months with the intention of excluding Islamist candidates and their supporters from participating," it added in a statement.

CHRLA said government officials prevented independent and opposition candidates and their representatives from being present during the voting and counting while NDP candidates were allowed to have several representatives at each committee.

The independent Egyptian Organisation for Human Rights said the government deprived thousands of their right to vote and to run by barring many from electoral lists and creating administrative obstacles ahead of registration.
Turnout was estimated by witnesses at not more than five percent but NDP members put it at between 40-50 percent.
